title.en: Tell a syntax error from an exception
Read the error message Python shows

say.en: Your program is typed perfectly, yet it stops the moment a user enters 0. Some errors are spelling mistakes in the code; others appear only while it runs. In this lesson: Tell a syntax error from an exception.
Read the error message Python shows.
Explain why exceptions need handling.

body.en: A *syntax* error happens when a statement breaks the rules of the Python language: a missing colon, a missing bracket or a misspelt keyword. Such errors are also called parsing errors. Python finds them while reading the code, so the program does not start until they are corrected. In the shell, Python shows the error name and a short description; in script mode, an error message points to the faulty line.

points.en: Must be corrected by the programmer

title.en: When does Python raise an exception?

narration.en: A syntax error stops the program before it runs. An exception happens while it runs, when a statement cannot be carried out: dividing by zero raises ZeroDivisionError, a bad list index raises IndexError. Wrapping the code in try/except lets the program handle it and continue. Set b to 0 with division. Then wrap it in try/except. What changes in the output? With nums[b], which values of b work? Why does −3 work but 3 not?
narration.kn: ಸಿಂಟ್ಯಾಕ್ಸ್ ದೋಷ ಪ್ರೋಗ್ರಾಂ ಚಾಲನೆಗೆ ಮೊದಲೇ ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ವಿನಾಯಿತಿ ಚಾಲನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ, ಒಂದು ಹೇಳಿಕೆ ನಡೆಸಲಾಗದಾಗ: ಶೂನ್ಯದಿಂದ ಭಾಗಿಸಿದರೆ ZeroDivisionError, ತಪ್ಪು ಸೂಚ್ಯಂಕ IndexError. try/except ಒಳಗೆ ಇಟ್ಟರೆ ಪ್ರೋಗ್ರಾಂ ನಿರ್ವಹಿಸಿ ಮುಂದುವರಿಯುತ್ತದೆ. ಭಾಗಾಕಾರದಲ್ಲಿ b = 0 ಮಾಡಿ. ನಂತರ try/except ಸೇರಿಸಿ. ಔಟ್‌ಪುಟ್ ಏನು ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ? nums[b]ಗೆ ಯಾವ b ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ? −3 ಏಕೆ ಸರಿ, 3 ಏಕೆ ಅಲ್ಲ?

title.en: On the board: When does each kind of error appear?

say.en: First Python reads, or parses, the whole program. A broken rule here is a syntax error, and nothing runs.
If parsing succeeds, the program starts to run.
An error during the run is an exception: dividing by zero, a missing file, or int of abc. Python creates an exception object.
If nobody handles the exception, the program stops with a traceback. Next we learn to handle it.

text.en: Unhandled → program stops with a traceback

narration.en: We follow a program from the moment Python reads it to the moment it runs, and see where syntax errors and exceptions appear.

say.en: We follow a program from the moment Python reads it to the moment it runs, and see where syntax errors and exceptions appear.

explanation.en: Syntax errors break the grammar of Python and are found before anything runs. Exceptions happen in correct code while it runs: division by zero, a bad conversion, a missing file or a bad index. 10 // 3 is 3 and "5" * 3 is "555".
explanation.kn: ವಾಕ್ಯರಚನೆ ದೋಷ ಚಲಿಸುವ ಮೊದಲೇ ಸಿಗುತ್ತದೆ. ವಿನಾಯಿತಿ ಸರಿಯಾದ ಕೋಡ್ ಚಲಿಸುವಾಗ ಬರುತ್ತದೆ.

say.en: Syntax error or exception? Sort each line of code.

body.en: Even when a statement is syntactically correct, something can go wrong while it executes: dividing by zero, opening a file that does not exist, or converting "abc" to a number. Such an error is an exception. In Python an exception is an object that represents the error. If no code handles it, the program stops abruptly and Python prints a traceback.

Programmers write exception handlers to deal with them

problem.en: Predict what happens when this script runs: print("Start"); x = 10; print(x / 0); print("End")  (four lines)

steps.en: There is no syntax error, so Python starts executing line by line.
Line 1 prints Start; line 2 assigns 10 to x.
Line 3 divides by zero, so a ZeroDivisionError exception is raised during execution.
The exception is not handled, so the program stops and line 4 never runs.

answer.en: Start is printed, then the traceback ends with ZeroDivisionError: division by zero; End is never printed.
